new_statements.quote: Grassfields languages, like the majority of Bantu, are tonal. One drawback to the decision to work primarily with simple citation-forms is that they fail to reveal the floating tones that are a characteristic feature throughout the Grassfields. [...] As already noted in §2.2.2, tone is distinctive in Grassfields languages and, as such, has been marked in the data. [...] Because a proper tone analysis has not been done on any of these languages other than Aghem, the marking system should not be looked on as anything more than an impression of pitch.

new_statements.relation_note: Group-level statement that the A810/Grassfields languages incl. Zhoa are tonal with distinctive tone; Zhoa data tone-marked impressionistically; also gives Zhoa segmental facts (eight consonants allowed in coda, /e o/ keep [e o] quality, root-final /p/ > [b~β] before vowel, te- class prefix etc.). No word-stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zhoa, with the other A810 (West Ring) languages Aghem, Bu, Isu and Weh, is treated as a tone language: tone is distinctive (Grassfields-wide, with floating tones), and every Zhoa form in the comparative series is transcribed with H/M/L/contour pitch marks, explicitly impressionistic because no tone analysis exists for any A810 language except Aghem. Nothing is said about word stress or accent in Zhoa; 'stress' occurs only in a diachronic hypothesis (p. 25/§1.5 area, 'schwa-effect on an unstressed prefix when followed by primary stress on the first syllable of the stem' in Pre-Bantu > A810 prefixes) and in a speculative remark on Aghem (p. ~133).
new_statements.exceptions: none for prosody; author warns mid-tone marks do not assert a phonemic Mid ('they likely do not' have one).
new_statements.identity_note: 'A810' = Aghem, Bu, Isu, Weh and Zhoa (ALCAM 810 'Aghem dialects', Menchum Division); the Zhoa data are first-hand: SIL Africa Area 1700-item wordlist recorded in Zhoa village in January 2004 by Nelson Tschonghongei & D. Thormoset for the Aghem Language Development Committee (§2.2.1, pp. 36-37); Zhoa = Glottolog zhoa1238 / ISO zhw (one village, Fungom subdivision; thesis p. 4 discusses the 1995 SIL survey's proposal to treat Zhoa as separate from A810 and rejects it on comparative grounds). Not on Glottolog's zhoa1238 reference list (may be filed under Aghem). The tone statements quoted are made for 'Grassfields languages' / 'these languages' (the five A810 languages incl. Zhoa) as a group, not for Zhoa individually; Zhoa forms throughout ch. 3 carry impressionistic tone marks.
